name: split_join_distance

scenarios.label: split_join_distance/small n=256 k=8
scenarios.note: Striped partition with every 7th vertex shifted by one cluster (mod k).

scenarios.label: split_join_distance/medium n=10000 k=100
scenarios.note: Larger striped pair, dense confusion matrix (≈k^2 nonzero cells).

scenarios.label: split_join_distance/subpartition n=10000 k=100
scenarios.note: Coarsening pair b = a/2: every a-cluster fits in one b-cluster ⇒ d12 = 0; exercises the one-side-dominates path.

summary.complexity: O(n) hashing + O(|nz|) row/col-max accumulation; |nz| ≤ min(k1·k2, n).
summary.memory: 1 HashMap<(u32,u32), u32> + 2 SmallVec-equivalent row/col-max scratch vectors of length k1, k2.

python_igraph_baseline.method_note: python-igraph exposes the symmetric scalar (d12+d21); the internal C cost is identical to returning the pair.

notes: All scenarios reuse the densified confusion-matrix machinery shared with compare_communities (CM-015).
Subpartition case has the same asymptotic cost as the perturbed striped case; the speedup ratio is preserved.
Rust path avoids the python-side dict/list marshalling overhead — the bulk of the python-igraph cost is in the FFI boundary, not in the C algorithm itself.
